findings.location: LESSONS.md (working tree) — the corrected entry is absent
findings.evidence: The corrected entry is NOT in the tree. `git diff --quiet HEAD -- LESSONS.md` exits clean; `git diff --stat` is empty; LESSONS.md is 337 lines in both the working tree and HEAD, and its last entry is the auic 'Regenerate a mechanical report' one -- the entry before the qnvo lesson. `grep -c 'sources: claude-workflow-plugin-qnvo' LESSONS.md` = 0. `lessons.sh list` reports total_ledger_entries=235 / evidence-tagged=114, against 236 / 115 measured in round 1 while the entry was present: one entry removed, none added. MECHANISM, from `git reflog --date=iso` on the MAIN working tree: 22:53:26 checkout v5/design-phase -> qnvo/primitive-replacement (a branch checkout CARRIES an uncommitted edit along, and LESSONS.md is identical in both commits so it transferred cleanly); 22:53:32 commit (amend) -> f94d80f; 22:54:07 checkout back to the branch at f94d80f; 22:54:11 `reset: moving to 1f4bd81`; 22:54:11 checkout back to v5/design-phase. The `git reset --hard 1f4bd81` ran in the MAIN working tree and discarded the uncommitted correction. NOT RECOVERABLE from git: the edit was never staged, so no blob was ever written -- `git fsck --lost-found` yields no LESSONS.md-shaped dangling blob (the only two blobs matching '139' are .beads/issues.jsonl exports, 190KB and 271KB, first line {"id":"claude-workflow-plugin-0pj"...}), and `git stash list` is empty. The near-miss note's 'tree verified identical, so nothing was lost' verified the COMMIT's tree -- I confirm f94d80f^{tree} == 1f4bd81^{tree}, so the amend touched the message only -- but the working tree was never checked, and that is where the correction lived.
findings.description: Round 2's fix is not in the change set. Nothing incorrect shipped, but nothing correct shipped either: with the entry gone, the reviewable content of this change set is now empty, and the ledger silently reverted to its pre-round-1 state. The false-negative that hid this is worth naming because it is the same shape as the original defect: `lessons.test.sh` 118/0 is TRUE and was read as confirmation, but it validates ledger GRAMMAR and passes identically on a ledger with no new entry -- a check that cannot fail for the thing it was taken to confirm. The prose must be re-authored; it cannot be restored. That is cheap, because the content survives in three places I verified: the f94d80f commit message (still reachable via reflog), the CORRECTION comment on this task, and the completion record's llm_observations, which carries the sharpened generalisation verbatim ('partially running a scan's list inherits the scan's blind spot while FEELING like measurement'). Re-add via `lessons.sh add --stdin --source claude-workflow-plugin-qnvo --tag evidence` with a quoted heredoc, then confirm presence with `grep -c 'sources: claude-workflow-plugin-qnvo' LESSONS.md` returning 1 and `lessons.sh list` reporting total=236 -- not with lessons.test.sh, which cannot answer that question.

findings.location: COMPLETION v1 record for claude-workflow-plugin-do5o, role=devops, payload_sha=8feea2ec
findings.evidence: The record attests `1 file(s)` with files_changed=[LESSONS.md]. Measured at 91b8e6d: LESSONS.md is byte-identical to HEAD and absent from `git diff --stat`. The only working-tree artifact is docs/reviews/claude-workflow-plugin-do5o-r1.json, which is my own round-1 review artifact, not the declared file.
findings.description: files_changed is the INDEPENDENT WITNESS that qa-gate.sh approve cross-checks against the change set it binds, and it is the one signal in the system that a change set is SHORT rather than merely stale. Here it attests a file change that does not exist, so the record asserts the fix landed when it did not. This is separable from R2-F1: F1 is the lost work, F2 is the record that would have let the loss pass unnoticed. Re-record the contract after the entry is genuinely re-added, and treat the declared-vs-actual comparison as a check to RUN rather than a field to fill.

findings.description: The comment-correction pattern is sound and auditable for the description -- an append-only correction preserves what was believed and when. The TITLE is the exception worth fixing directly: it is the only one of these fields that appears in `bd list` and in every ready-work query WITHOUT its comments, so the superseded 45/four figure is what a reader sees by default and the correction is invisible from there. This is a judgement call rather than a defect; the figure is superseded either way.
